verdict.winner: Modified bitumen wins on multi-ply toughness; TPO wins on reflectance and lower NJ install cost.
verdict.reasoning: Modified bitumen beats TPO when the roof carries frequent foot traffic or rooftop equipment because its 2-3 reinforced plies resist punctures and dropped tools that a single-ply membrane absorbs, per NRCA, where TPO needs walk pads in traffic lanes.
verdict.alternate: TPO beats modified bitumen when cooling load and install budget lead: TPO's white surface carries roughly 0.70-0.85 solar reflectance per CRRC against modified bitumen's heat-absorbing dark cap, and TPO installs at $8.00-$12.00 per NJ square foot, per Josten Roofing.

keyFacts: On the InterNACHI life-expectancy chart, modified bitumen rates 20 years versus TPO's 7-20 years (InterNACHI).
TPO is commonly cited at 15-25 years in practice, per Progressive Materials.
Modified bitumen is a multi-ply low-slope membrane that layers a polymer-modified asphalt cap sheet (SBS or APP modifier) over 2-3 reinforced base plies (gold definition).
TPO is a single-ply thermoplastic-polyolefin membrane, hot-air heat-welded at the seams, installed on commercial and residential low-slope/flat roofs (gold definition).
TPO installs at $8.00-$12.00 per NJ square foot, per Josten Roofing.

Modified bitumen falls inside the broader NJ flat-roof installed bracket of $2.50-$10.00 per square foot, per HomeGuide (no sourced standalone modified-bitumen per-foot figure, so no per-foot head-to-head winner holds).
TPO at $8.00-$12.00 per NJ square foot sits in the same low-slope band as EPDM ($7.00-$10.00) and PVC ($6-$12), per Josten Roofing.
NJ flat-roof pricing runs roughly 10-40% above national averages on higher labor and stricter code, per Josten Roofing.
Modified bitumen flat-roof repair runs $300-$1,100 for a typical job, with extensive leak-plus-structure work reaching $1,200-$3,000, per HomeGuide and Angi.
TPO seam re-welds run $200-$400 and patches $300-$500, per Modernize.

TPO's white surface carries roughly 0.70-0.85 initial solar reflectance and roughly 0.80-0.90 thermal emittance per ASTM C1549, CRRC-listed, while modified bitumen's dark granule cap absorbs solar load, per CRRC.
TPO reflectance reduces peak summer cooling demand 11-27% in air-conditioned buildings, per the EPA.

A reflective roof keeps its surface temperature over 50 degrees F below a conventional roof on a sunny afternoon, per the DOE; roof reflective performance is rated by reflectance and emittance, not R-value, per CRRC.

Modified bitumen withstands foot traffic better than TPO: its 2-3 reinforced plies form a thick membrane resisting dropped tools and rooftop-equipment placement, while single-ply TPO needs walk pads in high-traffic lanes, per NRCA.

Modified bitumen multi-ply construction provides redundancy so a surface gouge meets additional plies before reaching the deck, whereas a puncture breaches single-layer TPO outright, per NRCA technical guidance.
Modified bitumen fails by blistering, delamination, alligator cracking from UV oxidation, and flashing separation at penetrations, per NRCA.
TPO fails primarily by welded-seam failure plus thermal-shock cracking as plasticizers migrate and the membrane hardens, per NRCA.

Modified bitumen installs by torch-applied or cold-adhesive methods (cold-adhesive uses no open flame and costs slightly more than torch-applied), while TPO joins by hot-air heat-welded seams with no flame, per NRCA.

Neither modified bitumen nor TPO tolerates chronic ponding; NJ building code requires positive drainage, and tapered insulation under either membrane directs water to drains, with modified bitumen's multi-ply construction carrying slightly more ponding tolerance, per NRCA.

TPO can be installed over existing modified bitumen via a recover board in many NJ cases; the board separates membranes and adds insulation, with N.J.A.C. 5:23-6.4 limiting total roof layers, per the NJ Rehabilitation Subcode.
sources: NJ DCA (Department of Community Affairs) energy subcode
2021 IECC (adopted by NJ for ceiling insulation)
njContext: TPO installs at $8.00-$12.00 per NJ square foot, per Josten Roofing; modified bitumen falls inside the broader NJ flat-roof bracket of $2.50-$10.00 per square foot, per HomeGuide.
NJ flat-roof pricing runs roughly 10-40% above national averages on higher labor and stricter code, per Josten Roofing.

The NJ Uniform Construction Code treats a full re-roof of modified bitumen or TPO as ordinary maintenance on a detached 1- or 2-family dwelling: no permit, inspection, or notice, per N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7 and the NJ DCA.

The NJ UCC requires a permit once flat-roof work exceeds 25% of roof area within 12 months on a commercial, condo, or attached building, or turns structural by cutting load-bearing members, per N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7(b) and 5:23-2.7(c).
Newark sits in IRC Climate Zone 4A-5 (heating-dominated), which carries a winter heating offset that narrows the net annual reflectance benefit of a white TPO roof, per the DOE and EPA.
NJ adopted the 2021 IECC for ceiling insulation (R-60, Zones 4-5) but sets no cool-roof reflectance mandate for low-slope residential, per the DOE, EPA, and NJ DCA energy subcode.

TPO over existing modified bitumen via a recover board is allowed in many NJ cases, but N.J.A.C. 5:23-6.4 limits total roof layers and deck/layer count governs whether the recover qualifies, per the NJ Rehabilitation Subcode.

On a commercial NJ building, TPO (or modified bitumen) work triggers a UCC permit once it exceeds 25% of roof area in 12 months, since the ordinary-maintenance exemption covers only detached 1- and 2-family dwellings, per N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7(c).
positioning: Position Newark Quality Roofing as a registered New Jersey Home Improvement Contractor (registration under N.J.S.A. 56:8-136, not a 'license' since NJ issues no roofing license), insured, offering a free written estimate, that installs both modified bitumen and TPO on Essex County low-slope and flat roofs. Frame any warranty honestly as two separate parts: a manufacturer material warranty plus NQR's own written workmanship warranty; never reference manufacturer certification tiers (no GAF Master Elite, no CertainTeed SELECT, no 'we are certified' claims) and never invent project counts or field anecdotes. Recommendations are grounded in named standards and trade sources (NRCA, CRRC/ASTM C1549, InterNACHI, EPA/DOE, N.J.A.C. 5:23) rather than self-asserted experience.

buyersGuide.h1: Which Is Better: Modified Bitumen vs TPO?
buyersGuide.directAnswerThesis: Neither wins outright: modified bitumen (20-year InterNACHI rating, multi-ply) wins for heavy foot traffic and rooftop equipment; white TPO wins for cooling-load reflectance and lower NJ install cost ($8-12/sq ft).
sectionAngles: What does each membrane cost to install and repair on an Essex County flat roof? (TPO $8-12/sq ft per Josten Roofing vs modified bitumen inside the $2.50-$10 bracket per HomeGuide; repair ranges per HomeGuide/Modernize/Angi)

Which membrane fits Newark's climate and NJ flat-roof code? (TPO 0.70-0.85 reflectance/EPA 11-27% cooling reduction vs heating-offset Zone 4A-5; N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7 ordinary-maintenance vs commercial 25% permit rule)
How do you decide between them - what is the deciding factor? (foot traffic / rooftop equipment / puncture risk favors modified bitumen per NRCA; cooling load + budget favors TPO per CRRC/Josten)

expertPicks.h1: What Do NJ Roofers Recommend for Modified Bitumen vs TPO?
expertPicks.directAnswerThesis: The evidence favors white TPO for cooling-driven, low-traffic flat roofs (CRRC reflectance, lower NJ cost) and modified bitumen for equipment-heavy, high-foot-traffic roofs where its 2-3 reinforced plies resist punctures, per NRCA.
sectionAngles: What do the roofing standards actually favor for each roof profile? (NRCA foot-traffic/puncture redundancy for modified bitumen; CRRC/ASTM C1549 reflectance and EPA 11-27% cooling reduction for TPO)

Which installation and seam factors decide long-term performance? (modified bitumen torch vs no-flame cold-adhesive per NRCA; TPO hot-air welded seams whose welded-seam failure is its dominant failure mode per NRCA)

What flat-roof mistakes shorten membrane life in NJ? (ignoring ponding - neither tolerates it, NJ code requires positive drainage; skipping walk pads on single-ply TPO; over-stacking layers past N.J.A.C. 5:23-6.4 on recover jobs)
